requirement_text.REQ-035: GitHub issue #67. Organizer approve/reject surface for pending requests (admission='requested'), with reason, notification and logged capacity override. Implements USER-STORIES F3 / STORY-DETAILS F3 (Decide who comes in) plus PRD FR-13's approve/reject-with-reason. depends_on: REQ-034 (merged). An organizer lists PENDING requests for an event in their own chapter: company, position, student flag, source per row -- S3 forbids phone/email in this list, same constraint REQ-028's check-in list already carries. Filter/search for larger rooms. APPROVE: requested -> admitted, notify, issue qr_token via the EXISTING generateQrToken() in domain/registration.ts -- not a second generator. REJECT WITH REASON: requested -> rejected, notify respectfully with the reason AND an onward path -- this requirement's own WISHLIST OFFRAMP decision: Release 2 reuses REQ-017's upcoming-events list, exactly as REQ-027's cancellation message already does; NO Wishlist entity/table/migration/row is created (that is Release 3's G4, out of scope here). CAPACITY AT APPROVAL: approving when admitted count already equals capacity requires an EXPLICIT CONFIRMED override writing an AuditLog row -- the same override shape REQ-029 (check-in) and REQ-030 (walk-in) already implement; the design states whether the existing mechanism is reused or why not. The approval write is ATOMIC against the capacity check (S7) -- two organizers approving the last seat concurrently must not both succeed without an override; AC5 requires an automated concurrency test (20+ repeats, real Postgres, TEST-DESIGNER's scope later) but the design must name the exact locking/transaction mechanism. AUTHORIZATION (S2): requireOrganizerForChapter() (existing, domain/eventAuthorization.ts) checked ON THE HANDLER, not just the menu; EventStaff must be refused. PRIVACY (S3): the request list shows company/position/student/source and MUST NOT show phone or email, same as REQ-028's list. NOTIFICATIONS: both transactional (S10, sent regardless of broadcast_opt_in), through REQ-025's ledger, using the EXISTING 'admission_result' NotificationKind (domain/notification.ts) with a distinct kind per outcome so approve and a later state change cannot collide on one ledger key -- the design traces precisely what this requires. AUDIT: exactly one AuditLog row per approve/reject (S8).

task.description: WF-02 Step 1 (Design) for REQ-035, on branch feature/WF02-REQ-035 (verified branch matches). Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-035.md mapping all 10 acceptance criteria to concrete design elements: a new list read (listPendingRequestsForOrganizer, S3-safe by structural column exclusion, mirroring REQ-028's listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin), a new pure decision (decideApprovalOutcome) and transactional writer (approveRequest) that reuse REQ-030's overrideConfirmed-threading + SELECT...FOR UPDATE row-lock pattern (traced against REQ-020/023/030, NOT REQ-029's overrideAdmitAndCheckIn, with the distinction traced precisely: REQ-029 combines admit+checkin for a door-side QR refusal with no capacity gate at all, while REQ-035 needs a genuine capacity gate and must never touch checkedInAt/checkedInBy/checkInMethod), a parallel decideRejectionOutcome/rejectRequest pair, and both notification sends reusing the EXISTING 'admission_result' NotificationKind unchanged (traced why one kind suffices: a requested row transitions to admitted XOR rejected exactly once via this requirement's own two writers, so the (registration_id, kind) unique ledger index is never asked to hold two sends for the same row -- no new NotificationKind literal is added). Confirmed independently: no schema change (every write targets existing columns/types) -- DATA-DESIGNER is NOT needed for this run.
acceptance_criteria: Approving sets admission='admitted', issues a non-null qr_token via the existing generateQrToken(), and notifies the person.
Rejecting sets admission='rejected', notifies, and the captured message contains BOTH the organizer's stated reason AND an onward path pointing at the upcoming-events list.
No wishlist table, migration or row is created by this requirement, verified by grepping every migration and the schema for 'wishlist'.

Approving when admitted count already equals capacity requires an explicit confirmation: dismissing leaves admission='requested' unchanged; confirming sets 'admitted' AND writes exactly one audit_log row recording the override.

Two organizers approving the last remaining seat concurrently never produce an admitted count above capacity without an override -- verified by an automated concurrency test, 20+ repeats, real Postgres.
A member, and separately an EventStaff member for that same event, each invoking the approve handler DIRECTLY are both refused and the registration is unchanged.
An organizer of chapter A invoking the approve handler for a chapter B event is refused.
The rendered request list contains no phone number and no email address.
The approval and the rejection notification each reach a user with broadcast_opt_in=false.
Each approve and each reject writes exactly one audit_log row.

result.summary: Produced docs/agents/design/REQ-035.md (10 sections, full AC map in section 9, open questions in section 8). Key resolutions, each traced against actual code (not the issue's assertions taken on faith): (1) Concurrency mechanism = the same SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row-lock-on-events + fresh in-transaction re-count pattern REQ-020/REQ-023/REQ-030 already use -- named exactly, testable with a real-Postgres 20+-repeat concurrency test since the serialization is a database primitive, not an in-process mutex. (2) Capacity override reuses REQ-030's commitWalkin shape (a threaded overrideConfirmed boolean feeding a pure decision function, with a distinct audit-action string per branch: registration.approve vs registration.approve_override) -- explicitly NOT REQ-029's overrideAdmitAndCheckIn, because that function combines admit+checkin for a door-side QR-refusal scenario with NO capacity check at all (by its own design comment), which does not fit REQ-035's away-from-the-door, capacity-gated, non-checkin approval. (3) Notification kind: both approve and reject reuse the EXISTING 'admission_result' NotificationKind literal unchanged -- no second literal added -- because the notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) index is never asked to hold two admission_result sends for the same registration (a requested row transitions to admitted XOR rejected exactly once via this requirement's own two writers; no other code path in the codebase sends admission_result for an already-decided row, confirmed by reading both REQ-029's and REQ-030's override call sites, neither of which calls sendLedgeredNotification for the attendee at all). (4) List rendering mirrors REQ-028's listAdmittedRegistrantsForCheckin exactly: company/position/isStudent/source are selected; profiles.phone/profiles.email are structurally absent from the query's own select clause (S3). (5) Filter/search for 'larger rooms' reuses REQ-028's existing in-memory substring-filter + PAGE_SIZE/SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT mechanism -- no new filtering approach invented. (6) Zero Wishlist confirmed: only the existing catalog.event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming string is reused for the onward path, same as REQ-027's cancellation-notice precedent; no new table/migration/row of any kind is proposed anywhere in the design. No schema change anywhere in this design -- DATA-DESIGNER is NOT needed for this run.
issues: OPEN (named as Open Question 1 in the design, routed to whichever role owns it if a future requirement needs it): the organizer's rejection reason text is captured only in audit_log.payload and the notification text, not on a new registrations column -- no AC requires a stored, queryable rejection-reason field.

OPEN (Open Question 2): the exact plumbing location for reusing checkin.ts's PAGE_SIZE/SEARCH_RESULT_LIMIT constants (import as-is vs. hoist to a shared module) is left to BACKEND-DEV -- no behavioral consequence either way.

OPEN (Open Question 3): whether approve/reject on a since-cancelled or since-finished event needs a distinct refusal is NOT addressed by any AC in this requirement's list and is deliberately not silently added -- flagged for REQ-036 or a later requirement if it turns out to matter.

OPEN (Open Question 4): no AC requires an open list view in another organizer's session to auto-refresh after a decision elsewhere -- deliberately left unaddressed, same precedent REQ-028's own toggle handler already accepts for its stale-row case.

OPEN (Open Question 5): the exact mechanism for scoping 'the organizer's next text message' to one in-progress reject flow (grammY conversations plugin vs. an in-memory map vs. a stored pending-action row) is implementation, not design -- left to BACKEND-DEV.
